# The Consensus API

Written by Allison Elechko

October 12, 2026

The Consensus API lets you integrate Consensus search directly into your own applications, tools, and workflows. Use it to programmatically search academic research and retrieve relevant papers without needing to run each search manually in Consensus.

API access is available directly from your Consensus account. Your API usage and Consensus MCP usage share the same monthly pool of calls. The number of calls included each month depends on your subscription tier.

For full technical documentation, endpoints, parameters, and response details, read our API docs here.

# How to create an API key

You can create and manage API keys from the API & MCP Dashboard.

  1. Click your profile icon (bottom-left corner)

  2. Select API & MCP Dashboard

  3. Open the 'Keys and Clients' tab

  4. Click 'New key'

  5. Give your API key a name so you can identify what you're using it for

  6. Create the key and copy it somewhere secure

Your full API key is only shown once. Make sure you copy it when you create it.

If you lose an API key, you won't be able to view it again. Instead, revoke the existing key and create a new one.

Once you've created an API key, you can use it to authenticate requests to the Consensus API.

To make a search request, you'll need three things:

  1. The Consensus search endpoint: `https://api.consensus.app/v1/search`

  2. Your API key, passed in the `x-api-key` request header

pages.title: The Consensus API | The Consensus Help Center (https://help.consensus.app/en/articles/16516328-the-consensus-api)
pages.text: The Consensus API | The Consensus Help Center Skip to main content The Consensus API Written by Allison Elechko October 12, 2026 Table of contents The Consensus API lets you integrate Consensus search directly into your own applications, tools, and workflows. Use it to programmatically search academic research and retrieve relevant papers without needing to run each search manually in Consensus. API access is available directly from your Consensus account. Your API usage and Consensus MCP usage share the same monthly pool of calls. The number of calls included each month depends on your subscription tier. For full technical documentation, endpoints, parameters, and response details, read our API docs here . How to create an API key You can create and manage API keys from the API & MCP Dashboard. Click your profile icon (bottom-left corner) Select API & MCP Dashboard Open the ' Keys and Clients ' tab Click ' New key ' Give your API key a name so you can identify what you're using it for Create the key and copy it somewhere secure Your full API key is only shown once. Make sure you copy it when you create it. If you lose an API key, you won't be able to view it again. Instead, revoke the existing key and create a new one. Make your first API request Once you've created an API key, you can use it to authenticate requests to the Consensus API. To make a search request, you'll need three things: The Consensus search endpoint: https://api.consensus.app/v1/search Your API key, passed in the x-api-key request header A query parameter containing what you want to search for For example, if you want to search for research on whether creatine improves muscle strength, your request would send that question as the query to the Consensus search endpoint. If you're using a tool such as Postman, a programming language, or another application to make the request, add your Consensus API key as an x-api-key header. The API also supports filters that can help narrow your research, including publication date, study type, sample size, citation count, journal, academic field, country, open-access status, and more. For request examples and a full list of available parameters and responses, see the Consensus API Reference . Use the API to create and manage Threads In addition to standard paper search, the Consensus API can create and manage Threads. Threads are useful for more in-depth research tasks that require multi-step analysis, synthesis, and follow-up questions. Instead of only retrieving a list of papers, a Thread can generate a cited research answer with supporting papers and passages. With the Threads API, you can: Start a new Thread Poll a Thread until the response is ready Add a follow-up question to an existing Thread List historical Threads from your Consensus account Threads created through the API will also appear in your Consensus account. You can open them later in Consensus and continue working with them in the main interface. Thread usage is variable and counts toward your monthly API/MCP usage. A standard paper search typically uses fewer calls, while Threads may use more depending on the research mode, number of papers, and amount of work required. For implementation details and endpoint examples, see the Threads API documentation: https://docs.consensus.app/api-quickstart-threads Search and retrieve full text Consensus can use available full text, not just titles and abstracts, to help retrieve relevant papers. Paid users can also add include_full_text_chunks=true to a search request to return relevant passages from eligible open-access papers: Up to 3 passages per paper Up to 60 passages per request Each passage includes the section of the paper it came from If no eligible passage is available, full_text_chunks returns null Full-text retrieval is used when available on all plans. Returning full-text excerpts is available on Pro, Deep, Teams, and Enterprise plans. For request examples, full-text details, filters, and all available parameters, see the Consensus API documentation . How calls are counted API searches return up to 20 papers by default. You can use the page_size parameter to request more papers per page. Each call covers up to 100 papers: 1-100 papers = 1 call 101-200 papers = 2 calls 201-300 papers = 3 calls And so on, with each additional 100 papers counting as another call More advanced actions, such as creating a Consensus Thread, running a Pro or Deep Thread, or adding follow-up questions to a Thread, may use more calls depending on the amount of work required. Thread usage is variable because Consensus may run multiple research steps, search across more papers, read and synthesize results, and generate a cited response. You can view your usage from your profile > API & MCP Dashboard . The Usage tab shows activity by platform and tool, including searches, created Threads, Pro Threads, and Deep Threads. API and MCP usage limits API and MCP usage share one monthly pool of calls. Plan Included calls per month Maximum calls with additional usage ($0.05/call) Free 30 30 (no additional usage) Pro 500 1,000 Team 500 1,000 Enterprise 500 1,000 Deep 2,000 10,000 Additional usage costs $0.05 per call after you've used the calls included in your plan. Your usage resets on the 1st of each month. How to view your API and MCP usage To see your current usage: Click your profile icon in the bottom-left corner Select API & MCP Dashboard At the top of the dashboard, you'll see: Your current usage Any amount due for additional usage Your current plan and reset date The usage bar shows both the number of calls included in your plan and your total monthly call limit. The usage graph shows how your calls are split between API and MCP. You can view your usage for the last 7 days, last 30 days, or your current billing period. How to manage your API keys and MCP clients The Keys and Clients tab is where you manage both your API keys and MCP connections. API keys : you can create and revoke API keys MCP clients: you can connect Consensus to supported clients such as ChatGPT or Claude. If you've already connected a client, you'll see it here. How to enable additional usage Additional usage lets paid users continue making API and MCP calls after using all of the calls included in their plan. Additional usage is turned off by default. To enable it: Open the API & MCP Dashboard Select the settings control in the upper-right corner Under API & MCP settings, turn on Enable additional usage Save your changes Once enabled, calls beyond your plan's included amount are billed at $0.05 per call, up to your plan's maximum monthly call limit. You can turn additional usage off at any time. If you turn it off after you've already exceeded your included calls, you won't be able to make any more API or MCP calls until your usage resets. You'll still be billed for any additional calls made before you turned additional usage off. Free users cannot enable additional usage. To access additional usage, upgrade to a paid plan . Common API errors API Error message Cause Fix 401 - Invalid authentication credentials The API key is incorrect, revoked, or isn't being sent using the required header. Confirm you're using the correct API key in the x-api-key header. If you've lost the key, revoke it in the API & MCP Dashboard and create a new one. 402 - Billing past due Your subscription is past due, usually because a payment failed. API and MCP calls are paused until the billing issue is resolved. Update your payment method and resolve the outstanding payment to restore access. 429 - You've used all included {30, 500, 2,000, etc.} searches this month. Resets on {date}. You've used all of the API/MCP calls included in your plan. Paid users can enable additional usage from the API & MCP Dashboard, if they haven't reached their plan's maximum monthly call limit. Otherwise, wait until the reset date shown in the error message. 429 - Too many requests Requests are being sent faster than the current rate limit of one request per second. Slow down your requests and try again. Keep your API key secure Treat your API key like a password. Don't share it publicly or include it in publicly accessible client-side code, public repositories, screenshots, or other places where someone else could access it. If you believe a key has been exposed, revoke it from the API & MCP Dashboard and create a new one. You can manage your API keys, monitor API and MCP usage, review billing, and change your additional usage settings at any time from the API & MCP Dashboard. FAQs Where can I see my API/MCP billing history? Go to the API & MCP Dashboard, then click the Billing History tab. Do API and MCP have separate usage limits? No, your monthly usage limit is shared across API and MCP. What happens if I lose my API key? You won't be able to view the key again. Revoke the lost key and create a new one from the 'Keys and Clients' tab. pages.title: Getting Started with the Consensus MCP (https://docs.consensus.app/docs/mcp)
pages.text: Get started with Consensus MCP - Consensus Documentation Index Fetch the complete documentation index at: /llms.txt Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further. Skip to main content One hosted server covers every field of science, so you don’t need separate PubMed, OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar servers. Your assistant gets ranked papers it can filter by study design, sample size and journal quality, and cites real studies in its answers. Connect your client below. You’ll be searching in under 2 minutes. What you can build with the Consensus MCP MCP is the fastest way to give an assistant or agent paper search. Owkin plugged Consensus MCP into its agentic AI scientist and went from curated PubMed abstracts to 25x the paper coverage in days. Browse the use cases. Server URL https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp Claude Add Consensus from the Claude connectors directory. ChatGPT Add Consensus from the ChatGPT app directory. Microsoft 365 Copilot Add Consensus for Copilot from the Microsoft Marketplace. Perplexity Add Consensus from the Perplexity Computer connectors store. How Consensus compares In blinded evaluations on real user queries, Consensus search returns more relevant papers than Google Scholar and than frontier models with web search. See Benchmarks . More relevant than Google Scholar 88.1% vs 81.8% precision on 500 real user queries, judged blind by PhD researchers. Beats GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.8, 10x faster More relevant top-20 papers at a median of 8.7 seconds, versus 75 to 103 seconds. Connect Your Client Claude Desktop One-click: open Consensus in the Claude directory and click Connect . Or connect manually: 1 Open Settings Open claude.ai or the Claude desktop app and go to Settings . 2 Browse connectors Select Connectors , then Browse connectors . 3 Find Consensus Search for Consensus and click Connect . 4 Sign in Approve the sign-in with your Consensus account, or continue without one at reduced limits. 5 Start searching Ask a research question in any chat. Consensus appears in the tools menu. Claude Code claude mcp add --transport http consensus https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp OAuth will open in your browser automatically on first use. You can also trigger it manually with the /mcp command inside Claude Code. ChatGPT One-click: open Consensus in the ChatGPT app directory and click Connect . Or connect manually: 1 Open ChatGPT Open chatgpt.com and sign in. 2 Find Consensus Open Apps from the sidebar, search for Consensus , and click Connect . 3 Sign in Sign in with your Consensus account when prompted. 4 Start searching Ask a research question, or call it by name: “Use Consensus to find RCTs on…” Search results display in an interactive widget showing top papers with citations and direct links. Consensus also works with ChatGPT Deep Research. See Using Consensus with ChatGPT Deep Research below. Codex codex mcp add consensus --url https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp codex mcp login consensus Or add to ~/.codex/config.toml : [ mcp_servers . consensus ] url = "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp" Cursor One-click: Install in Cursor . Or add to ~/.cursor/mcp.json : { "mcpServers" : { "consensus" : { "command" : "npx" , "args" : [ "-y" , "mcp-remote@latest" , "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp" ] } } } VS Code (GitHub Copilot) Add to your MCP configuration: { "servers" : { "consensus" : { "url" : "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp" } } } Windsurf Add to your MCP configuration: { "mcpServers" : { "consensus" : { "serverUrl" : "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp" } } } Gemini Spark Add Consensus as a custom app for Gemini Spark: 1 Open Connected Apps Go to gemini.google.com and sign in with a personal Google Account, then click Settings & help → Connected Apps . 2 Add a custom app Under Custom apps for Spark , click Add a custom app and paste the server URL: https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp 3 Approve the connection Click Next and follow the prompts to finish OAuth. If your client doesn’t support Dynamic Client Registration, expand Advanced features and enter your credentials. 4 Start searching Ask Gemini Spark a research question and it can call Consensus tools. Requires access to Gemini Spark, a personal Google Account, Keep Activity turned on, and is currently available in the US. Workspace and school accounts are not supported yet. Perplexity 1 Open the Consensus connector Go to Consensus in the Perplexity connectors store . 2 Add the connector Click + Add Connector . 3 Sign in with Consensus Complete the OAuth sign-in with your Consensus account. You need a Consensus account , which is free to create. 4 Confirm the connection Click Connect on the OAuth confirmation screen. 5 Open Computer Click Computer . 6 Ask a research question Say “Use Consensus to…” followed by a scientific question, for example: “Use Consensus to identify the pros and cons of GLP-1s.” Microsoft 365 Copilot In Microsoft 365 Copilot, Consensus is a connector your admin sets up for the tenant. Once it’s there, connect it yourself under Sources . 1 Open Copilot Chat settings In Microsoft 365 Copilot, select the gear icon at the bottom of the left sidebar, then Settings , then Sources . 2 Connect Consensus Find Consensus for Copilot and select Connect , then sign in with your Consensus account. 3 Ask a research question Type a research question like ‘What does the research say about creatine and cognitive function?’ and Copilot will call Consensus to find relevant papers. Don’t see Consensus under Sources? Your admin needs to add it first. Send them the Microsoft 365 Copilot admin guide . A Consensus account is required and free to create. Microsoft 365 Copilot Studio This allows you to add Consensus as a custom tool in Copilot studio so it can be used with agents or other automations you have have. This type of authentication will 1 Open custom tools Go to Copilot studio and find the ‘tools’ tab on the left hand side. 2 Create 'Create new tool' Click ‘new tool’ to add a custom tool 3 Click 'Model context protocol' You can also use the API to do this. But to use the MCP, click ‘model context protocol’. 4 Fill in the connector information Server name Consensus Server Description Consensus is the go-to MCP for academic research. Search 400M+ scholarly articles, including 350M peer-reviewed papers, from PubMed, Semantic Scholar, and ArXiv — filter by study type (RCTs, meta-analyses, systematic reviews), journal quality, sample size, and more. Get structured results with citations, study takeaways, and direct links, or run pre-built workflows for literature reviews, grant research, and evidence synthesis. Server URL https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp Authentication OAuth 2.0 Type Dynamic Discovery 5 Save and use! Thats it! This custom tool can now be used and shared with other team members. Each team member will be able to connect to their own Consensus account when they use the tool. A Consensus account is required. It is free to create. API key (Bearer token) Use an API key for clients without OAuth, headless agents, and server-side automations. Send it in the Authorization header on every request to https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp : Authorization : Bearer YOUR_API_KEY Create a key from your profile icon under API & MCP Dashboard → Keys and clients → New key . The key gets its owner’s plan limits and draws from the same monthly pool as the API. See MCP plans and access . JSON config (Cursor, VS Code, and most clients that accept headers): { "mcpServers" : { "consensus" : { "url" : "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp" , "headers" : { "Authorization" : "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" } } } } Claude Code: claude mcp add --transport http consensus https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $CONSENSUS_API_KEY" An invalid or revoked key fails the search with a tool error: “Your API key is invalid or expired.” Create a new key from the API & MCP Dashboard and update your client config. Keep the key server-side. Don’t paste it into prompts or commit it to a repo. Other MCP clients Any client that supports remote MCP servers (Streamable HTTP) works. Point it at https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp . If your client supports OAuth, authentication is handled automatically. Pick your client for step-by-step setup. Watch: connect Consensus and run your first search Using Consensus with ChatGPT Deep Research Consensus also works with ChatGPT Deep Research. When Deep Research uses the Consensus app, it can search Consensus for relevant papers and retrieve full paper details for cited results. 1 Connect the Consensus app Connect the Consensus app in ChatGPT using the steps above. 2 Start a Deep Research request Start a Deep Research request in ChatGPT. 3 Ask ChatGPT to use Consensus Ask ChatGPT to use Consensus for peer-reviewed research, for example: Use Consensus to research the evidence on exercise for depression. Prioritize systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and randomized controlled trials. Deep Research may run multiple Consensus searches, refine filters, retrieve paper details, and return a cited synthesis with direct links to papers on Consensus. Verify Your Connection Try one of these in your connected client. Each link opens the question pre-filled: Ask Try it ”What does the research say about creatine and cognitive function?” Claude · ChatGPT ”Find meta-analyses on mindfulness for anxiety published since 2020” Claude · ChatGPT ”Are there RCTs on intermittent fasting with more than 500 participants?” Claude · ChatGPT ”What is the strongest evidence for and against remote work productivity?” Claude · ChatGPT You should see results citing specific papers with titles, journals, years, citation counts, and direct links. Plans and Access Your Consensus plan, not your AI subscription, sets how many papers each search returns, your monthly calls, whether results include DOIs and full-text excerpts, and whether Threads can use deep mode. No account is needed to try it. Plans and access Limits for every plan, how calls are counted, additional usage, and API key access. Tools Consensus MCP exposes six tools. Your assistant picks the right one from your question. Tool What it does search Find ranked, peer-reviewed papers for a query in one call. get_full_text Read the complete text of open-access papers from search results or Threads, as Markdown. create_thread Start a Thread: hand a research question to the Consensus research agent. get_thread Poll a Thread and read the agent’s cited answer. add_to_thread Ask a follow-up in an existing Thread. find_threads List your Threads and find an earlier one. search works without an account. The thread tools need a signed-in Consensus account or an API key. get_full_text needs a paid plan. Quick start: Search & Threads When to use search, when to start a Thread, and how a Thread runs. Troubleshooting OAuth login is only supported for streamable HTTP servers (Codex) You added the server with -- --transport http instead of --url . Remove and re-add: codex mcp remove consensus codex mcp add consensus --url https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp codex mcp login consensus Authentication successful but server reconnection failed (Claude Code) Fully quit and restart Claude Code. Do not just use the reconnect option. Your credentials are saved and will work after restart. Tools stop working after a few hours (401 errors) Your OAuth token has expired. Re-authenticate: Claude Code: Type /mcp , select Consensus, choose Clear authentication, re-authenticate, then restart Claude Code Codex: Run codex mcp logout consensus then codex mcp login consensus Cursor: Disconnect and reconnect the server in Settings then Tools and MCP Claude Desktop: Disconnect and reconnect the connector in Settings then Connectors ChatGPT: Disconnect and reconnect the Consensus app from ChatGPT Apps Perplexity: Disconnect and reconnect Consensus in Computer then Connectors Server shows failed or no tools appear Verify the URL includes /mcp at the end Remove and re-add the server using the commands above Restart your client completely Consensus search has not been loaded yet (Claude Code) This is normal. Claude loads tool definitions on demand when many tools are present. Retry the query and it will work on the second attempt. ChatGPT Deep Research is not using Consensus Confirm the Consensus app is connected in ChatGPT Apps, then ask Deep Research to use Consensus explicitly. For example: Use Consensus to find peer-reviewed papers on this question and cite the strongest evidence. Deep Research decides when to call connected tools, so it may not call Consensus for questions that are not research-focused. No results found Try broadening your search query or removing filters. Use specific academic terminology rather than casual language. Monthly call limit reached Paid plans can continue making calls past the included monthly limit when the account has an active metered API subscription and additional usage is enabled; extra usage is billed at $0.05 per call, with each call covering up to 100 papers. Free plans must wait for the next monthly reset or upgrade. Rate limit exceeded (429 error) Rate limits are per user for authenticated MCP clients. A 429 that says you’re sending requests too quickly is a per-minute rate limit; wait a few moments and add backoff between requests. A 429 that mentions monthly call credits is a usage limit, not a rate limit. Security Endpoint: Only connect to the official URL: https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp API keys: Store securely using environment variables. Never share keys in prompts or public conversations. Rotate if compromised. Data handling: Search queries are sent to the Consensus API over HTTPS/TLS. Results contain publicly available academic paper metadata. No personal data is stored from MCP requests. Supported Platforms Platform Auth Status Claude Desktop OAuth Supported ChatGPT OAuth Supported ChatGPT Deep Research OAuth Supported Claude Code OAuth Supported Codex OAuth Supported Cursor OAuth Supported VS Code (GitHub Copilot) Config Supported Windsurf Config Supported Gemini Spark OAuth Supported Perplexity OAuth Supported Other MCP Clients Bearer token Supported FAQ Is there a PubMed MCP server with semantic search? Yes. Consensus covers all of PubMed plus the rest of science, ranked semantically rather than by keyword match alone. You can filter by study design, sample size, journal quartile and citation count. See Where the papers come from . What's the best MCP server for scientific literature in Claude? Consensus is in the Claude connectors directory and works in Claude on the web, the Claude desktop app and Claude Code . How do I add a scientific search connector to ChatGPT? Connect Consensus from the ChatGPT app directory . It also works with ChatGPT Deep Research . Can I use a research paper search MCP server in Cursor or VS Code? Yes. Install it in one click in Cursor , or add the server URL to your MCP configuration in VS Code (GitHub Copilot) . Which MCP server works for pharma and drug discovery? Consensus is SOC 2 Type II compliant, doesn’t use customer data to train AI models, and offers a zero-data-retention option on enterprise agreements. It runs behind AI gateways and in Microsoft 365 Copilot . Owkin uses it in its agentic AI scientist. See Security and data handling . Does it work for systematic reviews and meta-analyses? Yes. Filter by study design, including RCTs, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, and run deep literature reviews with Threads. See the Threads quick start . Is this the same as Consensus (goconsensus.com)? No. This is Consensus, the AI academic search engine at consensus.app . It’s unrelated to the sales demo platform at goconsensus.com. Additional Resources Consensus Website Explore the Consensus research platform. API Documentation Structured JSON results for pipelines and integrations. MCP Specification Learn more about the Model Context Protocol. MCP server on GitHub View the source, report issues, and star the Consensus MCP server.
